title: Peeling Back the Layers of PowerShell Loader: Tracing a Multi-Stage Windows Payload Chain
content_md: By Aditya K Sood and Bikash Dash | November 2, 2026 Aryaka Threat Research Lab analyzed a multi-stage Windows malware infection chain that starts with a PowerShell loader associated with get.activated.win and leads to a protected native payload. The malware uses environment-aware execution, layered cryptographic processing, and in-memory payload reconstruction to conceal its final execution stage. A multi-stage PowerShell loader can turn a seemingly harmless Windows script into malware. It retrieves or embeds an obfuscated payload, then decodes and decrypts content, drops files, establishes persistence, and runs the final payload, potentially contacting command-and-control (C2) infrastructure. Staging helps attackers evade signature-based detection, hinder forensic investigations, and bypass defenses. The attack can lead to credential theft, data exfiltration, ransomware, and lateral movement, so defenders should trace the full execution chain rather than investigate the initial command alone. Threat Campaign Overview The infection begins with a PowerShell-based loader that retrieves a native payload from srv.conti.pk.
